auth.notes: Robot-to-cloud auth uses the client_token_guid issued at onboarding; the subscription is an account-level entitlement checked server-side. wire-pod issues the GUID locally and never contacts DDL.

cloud.failure_mode: Without a paid membership the robot loses cloud-processed voice commands ("Hey Vector" intents) and ChatGPT connectivity; DDL also gates the onboarding token exchange behind its account system. Local gRPC control is unaffected once a GUID has been issued. As of 2026-07-31 the official OTA/firmware hosts fail DNS entirely, while anki.bot continues to bill subscriptions ($11.99/mo or $99.99/yr per robot, verified 2026-08-04).
cloud.notes: Every cloud-dependent function has a local replacement: wire-pod substitutes for chipper (voice intents), TMS (token/GUID issuance) and jdocs (settings storage), so `required` is false for an owner willing to run it.
cloud.vendor_service: DDL Vector AI Subscription (chipper voice processing, TMS token service, jdocs)

device.name: Vector Robot
device.notes: Desktop companion robot with primary local control over WiFi using gRPC and protobuf 3 over TLS on port 443. Discovery uses mDNS service _ankivector._tcp.local. Connections require robot certificate pinning and a GUID bearer token obtained during onboarding. BLE onboarding uses Anki RTS protocol with CLAD serialization and libsodium encryption (crypto_kx + XChaCha20-Poly1305). The anki_vector Python SDK is available under Apache 2.0 and documents the ExternalInterface service. DDL is widely reported defunct since ~2023 and all official OTA/firmware servers fail DNS (tested 2026-07-31), so robots can no longer pull official OTAs; the anki.bot support portal remains online and still sells Vector AI subscriptions ($11.99/mo or $99.99/yr per robot, verified 2026-08-04 via anki.bot and support.anki.bot article 344). Latest official firmware is 2.0.1.6076 (Vector 2.0 + Gen 1, 2022-09-26); 1.8.1.6051 was the last Gen-1 production build. The dominant community path is wire-pod (kercre123/wire-pod, MIT, 778 stars at verification 2026-08-04), a full local voice server built on DDL's open-sourced vector-cloud that restores voice commands on production Vector 1.0/2.0 robots with no DDL subscription; production robots take a recovery-mode detour (Web Bluetooth flash of DDL's production-signed Escape-Pod-compatible "ep" firmware, then a user-data reset, then local authentication). Packaged installers ship from the separate kercre123/WirePod releases repo (v1.2.18, 2026-05-10: Windows .exe, macOS .dmg, Debian/Ubuntu .deb for amd64/arm64/armhf, Android .apk). For unlocked (OSKR/dev) robots, WireOS (os-vector/wire-os, 3.0.1.32 at verification time) is the fully open firmware option. DDL open-sourced vector-cloud (MIT) and vector-bluetooth before disappearing. In September 2024 the Pennsylvania AG sued DDL and its CEO over more than $4M in unfulfilled robot orders (~14,000 orders Nov 2020-Jan 2024; allegations, not adjudicated). The original companion app (com.anki.victor) is no longer fetchable: APKPure lists the package id with zero downloadable versions, and APKMirror and APKCombo have no copy (checked 2026-08-04) — the Web Bluetooth setup pages are the practical onboarding route now.

credentials.notes: The passphrase is sent as plaintext inside the encrypted BLE session, so confidentiality depends on the handshake having been completed with the on-screen PIN rather than on the field itself.
stored_on_device: WiFi credentials for each provisioned network

factory_reset.effect: Clear User Data wipes WiFi credentials, the owner/account association, enrolled faces and the issued client GUID. The ESN (serial) is hardware identity and survives, so the mDNS name and BLE advertisement stay the same. Do not confuse the two button procedures: holding the backpack button ~15 s boots Firmware Recovery Mode (factory firmware, shows anki.com/v, KEEPS user data), while Clear User Data is a separate menu path (DDL support articles 383 and 384).

procedures.indicator: Diagnostics menu appears; after confirming Clear User Data the robot reboots into onboarding (ddl.io/v setup screen).
procedures.name: Clear User Data menu (double-click backpack button)

steps.action: Place the robot on the charger.
Double-click the backpack button to open the diagnostics menu.
Navigate the menu with the lift and treads to Clear User Data and confirm.
Wait for the reboot; the robot returns to BLE pairing mode.

procedures.indicator: Screen shows anki.com/v; robot boots the factory recovery firmware without deleting user data.
procedures.name: Firmware Recovery Mode (recovery only, keeps user data)

steps.action: Place the robot on the charger.
Press and hold the backpack button for about 15 seconds until the recovery screen appears.

ble.pin_source: Six-digit PIN rendered on the robot's face display during pairing mode.
ble.protocol: Anki RTS (CLAD over BLE, XChaCha20-Poly1305 after handshake)

methods.description: Anki RTS over BLE: handshake, PIN confirmation, WiFi scan, credential push, then certificate/GUID retrieval. Versions 2 through 5 of the protocol all carry the same WiFi messages.

steps.action: Place the robot on its charger and double-click the backpack button to enter pairing mode.
steps.expect: Robot advertises as Vector-XXXX and shows a PIN on its screen.

steps.action: Connect and complete the RTS handshake (RtsConnRequest / RtsConnResponse / RtsNonceMessage / RtsChallengeMessage).
steps.expect: RtsChallengeSuccessMessage; all later traffic is XChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypted.

steps.action: Request a WiFi scan and present the results to the user.
steps.expect: RtsWifiScanResponse listing SSID, signal, auth type, hidden and provisioned flags.
RtsWifiConnectResponse carrying the resulting WiFi state and connect result.

arguments.description: SSID hex-encoded, not raw text — the field carries the hex string itself.
arguments.name: wifi_ssid_hex

arguments.description: Passphrase in the clear inside the already-encrypted BLE channel.
arguments.name: password

arguments.description: Seconds the robot should spend attempting the join before reporting failure.
arguments.name: timeout

arguments.description: Set when joining a hidden (non-broadcast) SSID.
arguments.name: hidden

steps.action: Read back the assigned address to confirm the join.
steps.expect: RtsWifiIpResponse with an IPv4 address; the robot now answers _ankivector._tcp.local.

steps.action: Exchange a session token for the long-lived control GUID.
steps.expect: client_token_guid returned; store it with the robot's certificate for gRPC sessions.
steps.notes: Only cloud-dependent step. wire-pod issues the token locally instead.

setup.notes: Vector is the best-documented onboarding flow in this repository because the BLE provisioning protocol (RTS) is published under Apache 2.0. WiFi credentials never touch a vendor server: they travel over an encrypted BLE channel established by a Curve25519 exchange, with a PIN shown on the robot's own screen as the proof of physical possession. Only the last step — trading a session token for the control GUID — has a cloud dependency, and wire-pod replaces it.

rejoin.notes: Moving Vector to a new network never needs a factory reset. Re-enter BLE pairing mode and send a fresh RtsWifiConnectRequest; RtsWifiForgetRequest drops one stored network or all of them. Because BLE works regardless of WiFi state, the robot is recoverable even after the old network is gone — the failure mode that strands most WiFi-only devices.

steps.action: Enter BLE pairing mode and complete the RTS handshake.
Optionally clear stale networks with RtsWifiForgetRequest.
Send RtsWifiConnectRequest for the new network.

covers: full gRPC ExternalInterface control (69 RPCs) and REST gateway on the LAN
voice commands via local wire-pod (Vosk STT by default; no audio leaves the LAN unless a remote STT/LLM plugin is configured)
onboarding, re-provisioning and GUID issuance without any vendor account
firmware freedom on unlocked robots via WireOS
not_covered: DDL's ChatGPT integration and any future cloud-only features — tied to the paid membership
official OTA updates — the vendor OTA hosts no longer resolve; wire-pod/WireOS are the update path
local_access.notes: Remaining friction on the production path, per the wire-pod wiki: Chrome/Chromium-only Web Bluetooth (chrome://flags experimental features on some builds; Linux may need the Bluetooth panel actively discovering), unsigned installers (SmartScreen, unidentified macOS developer, Android unknown-sources/Play Protect), and an authentication step that the wiki itself warns may need several ~20-second-spaced retries. The original companion app com.anki.victor is no longer fetchable from APKPure, APKMirror or APKCombo (checked 2026-08-04), so the Web Bluetooth pages are the de facto onboarding client.
local_access.summary: Vector speaks gRPC over TLS on the LAN as shipped; the only vendor-cloud steps were voice-intent processing and the onboarding token exchange, and wire-pod replaces both. For production robots the wire-pod path requires one firmware detour: boot recovery mode, pair over Web Bluetooth in Chrome, and accept DDL's production-signed Escape-Pod-compatible "ep" OTA (free, no Escape Pod purchase), then clear user data and authenticate against the local wire-pod instance. Unlocked (OSKR/dev) robots can instead run the fully open WireOS.

ble_onboarding.encryption: libsodium crypto_kx (Curve25519) key exchange, PIN mixed into session keys via crypto_generichash, crypto_aead_xchacha20poly1305_ietf (XChaCha20-Poly1305) session cipher
ble_onboarding.name: RTS
